title: Joining Piron's band after Paul Barbarin, and the alley
summary: Barbarin's departure from Piron's band opened the job for Frazier; talk of Robichaux and an alley bar.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands

blocks.x: Yeah, yeah, separated tumscrew rods. And then the later years, I went in from, let's see, it was 28, when I was working, John Robichauds, he had another dance orchestra. We used to play it, locally work around, you know, country club the same way, evening dances, night dances. It was like the Young Tuxedo Band. And during that year of, 20, later part of 1928, I was the, Paul Barbaran, when Lloyd Contrell died, the old drummer, he died, Paul Barbaran went into P-Round's band and he played a while him and his fellow by the name of Walter Pichauds and they formed the Pelicans of Silvertone Orchestra, Gravy and Ramport. And it was, consisted of Walter Pichauds and Paul Barbaran and it was, let's see, he was playing the David Jones saxophone and Manuel Sayles guitar, banjo. I just remember all the men that present, but I mean it's, and then he was in P-Round's band and he left the band at 28th and I met some of P-Round's bands at the place they call the Old Alley. They used to be on Seminard and Robert, next to the Seminard Market. And he was on the St. Joseph night when he asked me do I want to join the P-Round band because he was leaving the band on two weeks' notice.
No, that was Paul Barbaran. Paul Barbaran. Paul Barbaran.
Oh, to get back to that alley, once George Lewis made some records and they called them Eclipse Alley 5, was that called Eclipse Alley or?

Well, you see, they had Maurice Durand was playing the band in the alley during them days. He had a band in there with Maurice on trumpet and it was Dodden playing banjo and you had the drum at that time was working and it was I believe I think it was I think it was Ellie Bigard or I think it was Ellie Bigard playing drum in there and doing them.
I wonder, was there really a little alley there?

It was an alley right next to the market between the market and this old Seminard Market and a place they called used to have a driver's plug next to it but it was like an alley and the bottom sat way in the rear.

Facing like uptown. Yeah, I was at a riverside of Seminard Avenue like we call this Facing Uptown. Yeah, Facing Uptown. Yeah, that was way around well that stuff began around in the 20s too but it was during the year 1928. You know in fact before that happened we had played at a carnival party at the New Orleans Country Club with two bands it was A.J. Pirone band and John Robichaud band I was connected with John Robichaud band and they heard me play and at that same time when Paul was leaving the band I was the man it was choice for their band they liked my style of playing and they asked me to join that band and I had to go I joined that band the same year it was 1920 beginning of the month of February right after the conference season.
